$comment: Accepted survivors for scripts/mutation-check.mjs (#134): mutants on changed lines of .claude/hooks/*.mjs or scripts/*.mjs that no test kills because the change is equivalent (behaves the same) or is harmless over-refusal (the guard refuses more, never less). An entry matches on file, mutator, original and replacement text (whitespace collapsed), not on line number. Each entry needs a reason. The check prints a ready-made entry for every new survivor; add one only after deciding a test cannot or should not catch it. A survivor that lets the guard allow a command it should refuse is never accepted: add a test. See docs/quality.md.

survivors.reason: Equivalent: git quotes a diff path that contains a double quote, so a path from git ends in a quote only when it also starts with one.
Equivalent in readJson: with no encoding readFileSync returns a Buffer, and JSON.parse reads it as UTF-8 text, so the parsed ledger or report is the same.
Equivalent: with GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY unset, appendFileSync(undefined) throws and the catch ignores it, so nothing is written either way and the exit status does not change.

Equivalent: the only program spawned is process.execPath, the running Node binary, with a cwd git diff has just run in, so spawn never emits 'error' and the handler never runs. It stays so a failed start ends the check with exit 2 instead of an unhandled 'error' crash.

closeParen() (akmods#215 reader): equivalent for `const cases = []`. A string at the bottom of the stack has no depth, so it is never the case at the current depth and the pop loop stops at it; every real case is pushed above it and read as before.

closeParen() (akmods#215 reader): equivalent at each of its false literals. `let wordAtCommand = false` is overwritten by the first character of every word before it is read. `atCommand = false` after a case subject word, after `case` and after `esac`: subject and pattern words never read atCommand, the `)` that ends a pattern sets it again, and after `esac` bash allows only an operator or a redirection, so no case can open there on a line bash runs. `plain = false` and the false isPlain arguments: a word that is not plain always holds the backslash, quote or `$'` text that marks it, so it can never equal `case`, `esac`, `in` or a reserved word anyway.
closeParen() (akmods#215 reader): equivalent on lines bash runs: the second word of a case subject is always `in`; any other word there is a syntax error, so bash runs nothing.

closeParen() (akmods#215 reader): equivalent in the `esac` test: subject words are handled by the branch before it, and in a clause body patternRead is always true (the `)` that starts a body follows a pattern word or a `(`; `case a in ) b;; esac` is a syntax error).

closeParen() (akmods#215 reader): equivalent on lines bash runs: a case left open in a clause body reads every word and separator as no case does, except `;;`, `;&` and `;;&`, which bash allows only inside a case. Those then belong to an enclosing case, and the stale case takes its place one level down, so each `)` still ends the same pattern or the same substitution.

closeParen() (akmods#215 reader): equivalent in the `esac` test: no case is ever in state "", so this is the same as dropping the clause-body arm, which is accepted above (`top.state === 'body' && wordAtCommand` -> false).

closeParen() (akmods#215 reader): equivalent on lines bash runs, in the separator branch: a `)` inside a substitution or group in a case pattern (`case a in $(echo a)) b;; esac`) is read as the pattern's end and the pattern's own `)` as closing that inner level, so depth and case state agree again after the pattern. Words in between use endWord()'s own depth test, and `;;` cannot appear there.

closeParen() (akmods#215 reader): equivalent on lines bash runs: a case still open when the `)` of its own level closes is unterminated, a syntax error. The pop itself is covered: the `$( (case a in a) b) )` row hangs without it.
